g1|variants|scheduling agreements.family_title: SAP S/4HANA OTC Scheduling Agreements Family
g1|variants|scheduling agreements.summary: Scheduling agreements are long-term sales agreements with a customer covering predetermined total quantities or values over a specific timeframe, fulfilled via scheduled delivery releases. The family spans standard scheduling agreements without delivery control, with delivery control (LF/LPC), value-based contracts, and external EDI-driven releases.

variants.name: Standard Scheduling Agreement with Delivery Schedule (LP)
variants.when_used: Used for recurring customer deliveries with precise delivery dates and quantities tracked via scheduling lines.
variants.key_config: Sales Document Type LP configured with delivery schedule function enabled, schedule line categories CP assigned to item category TAN.

variants.name: Scheduling Agreement with External Delivery Schedule (LPA)
variants.when_used: Automated high-volume automotive or high-tech scenarios using EDI DELINS/DELFOR for JIT and Forecast delivery schedules.
variants.key_config: Sales Document Type LPA configured for release documentation, processing both forecast and JIT delivery schedules from EDI inbound.

variants.name: Value-Based Scheduling Agreement (MV)
variants.when_used: Long-term agreements where fulfillment is controlled by target monetary value rather than physical quantities.
variants.key_config: Document type MV tied to value item category WVN with value contract constraints activated in schedule line configuration.

g1|core|scheduling agreements|standard s.title: Standard Scheduling Agreement with Delivery Schedule (LP)
g1|core|scheduling agreements|standard s.story: Imagine a milkman who leaves a bottle at your porch every single Tuesday without you having to call him every week. In SAP, a scheduling agreement is a long-term sales contract with a customer that contains delivery quantities and dates spread over a timeline, allowing you to automatically generate deliveries when the dates arrive.
g1|core|scheduling agreements|standard s.why_business_needs_it: It secures long-term business commitments from key customers while smoothing out production and shipping schedules. Without it, sales teams would drown in manual repetitive order entry for recurring blanket purchase orders.

g1|core|scheduling agreements|scheduling.title: Scheduling Agreement with External Delivery Schedule (LPA)
g1|core|scheduling agreements|scheduling.story: Imagine a milk delivery truck that drops off bottles to a coffee shop every single Tuesday without the owner needing to call and order every time. In SAP S/4HANA, the Scheduling Agreement with External Delivery Schedule (document type LPA) is a long-term sales agreement where customers send periodic release documents to pull exact quantities on specific dates.
g1|core|scheduling agreements|scheduling.why_business_needs_it: High-volume manufacturers and suppliers use scheduling agreements to handle recurring customer demands without repeatedly creating standard sales orders. This streamlines delivery forecasting, material requirements planning (MRP), and delivery-related billing while maintaining a firm legal framework.

modules.role: Manages scheduling agreement creation, sales scheduling lines, delivery creation, and billing.
modules.hands_off_to: LE-SHP to generate outbound deliveries based on scheduling agreement release dates.

modules.role: Executes picking, packing, and goods issue processing for delivery type LF triggered by scheduling agreements.
modules.hands_off_to: FI-AR for customer invoice creation and revenue recognition.

g1|core|scheduling agreements|value-base.title: Value-Based Scheduling Agreement (MV) in Order-to-Cash
g1|core|scheduling agreements|value-base.story: Think of a regular purchase contract as an open promise to buy a specific dollar amount of goods over time without locking in exact dates yet. In SAP S/4HANA Order-to-Cash, a Value-Based Scheduling Agreement (MV) allows a customer to issue target values and delivery schedules where billing is triggered directly by order activities. If this setup is missing, your sales representatives cannot process high-level financial commitments tied to recurring fulfillment schedules.
g1|core|scheduling agreements|value-base.why_business_needs_it: It enables long-term business relationships where customers commit to a total target value rather than strict individual quantities per line item. It streamlines order processing by integrating target-value monitoring with direct order-related billing workflows.

g1|panel|scheduling agreements.otc_impact: Scheduling agreements sit at the long-term contract end of Order-to-Cash, bridging recurring customer demand and execution by transforming repetitive release schedules into scheduled deliveries, direct outbound deliveries, and periodic billing. They stabilize warehouse picking, transportation planning, and revenue forecasting by securing multi-period volumes while updating customer receivables and cash flow through seamless delivery-related billing. When schedules fail or unconsumed quantities linger, order processing stalls, deliveries miss customer dock windows, and Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) degrades due to blocked or delayed invoicing.

panel_qa.question: How do we choose between LP with internal delivery schedules and LPA with external EDI-driven delivery schedules for our high-volume automotive customers?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Scheduling agreements manage long-term framework orders with variant delivery types where LP uses manual schedule lines in transaction VA32, and LPA processes inbound EDI 830 or DELFOR releases via IDoc message type DELINS. We configure document types LP and LPA in Customizing under Sales and Distribution (SD) -> Sales -> Sales Documents -> Sales Document Header -> Define Sales Document Types, assigning appropriate delivery types LF and schedule line categories LA or C1. This setup automates high-frequency release processing, lowering administrative overhead and preventing stockouts at customer plants, thereby protecting critical on-time in-full (OTIF) KPIs. Next, we ensure outbound delivery monitor transaction VL04 runs smoothly against these release horizons. The weak answer is stating we use LP for everything because scheduling agreements are identical regardless of how the schedule is entered.
panel_qa.trap: The weak answer is stating we use LP for everything because scheduling agreements are identical regardless of how the schedule is entered.

panel_qa.question: What prevents unfulfilled quantities from accumulating at the validity end date of a scheduling agreement, and how do we handle value-based agreements like MV?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Value-based scheduling agreements type MV track target values instead of physical quantities, requiring specific item categories and pricing conditions that aggregate cumulative invoiced values against a ceiling. We configure these via SD -> Sales -> Sales Documents -> Sales Document Items -> Define Item Categories, ensuring billing relevance indicator B (delivery-related billing) or F is correctly mapped. This prevents revenue leakage by automatically halting further deliveries when the target value is reached, safeguarding profit margins on fixed-price service contracts. Next, we implement schedule line control using transaction VA33 to monitor cumulative delivered quantities against target quantities. The weak answer is assuming value-based agreements process like standard quantity contracts without monitoring cumulative target values.
panel_qa.trap: The weak answer is assuming value-based agreements process like standard quantity contracts without monitoring cumulative target values.

panel_qa.question: What is the financial impact on DSO and revenue recognition when inbound EDI delivery schedules fail to parse correctly in LPA processing?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: When inbound DELFOR IDocs fail with syntax errors or unmapped partner profiles in transaction WE02, schedule lines are not updated, halting outbound delivery creation in transaction VL10V. We resolve this by enforcing robust error handling via transaction BD87 and configuring ALE (Application Link Enabling) distribution models alongside partner profiles in transaction WE20. This automation eliminates manual order entry delays, ensuring goods issue triggers timely billing and accelerates cash collection. Next, we establish workflow alerts for inbound IDoc failures to protect monthly revenue forecasts. The weak answer is claiming IDoc failures do not impact cash flow because warehouse operations can ship goods without valid schedule lines.
panel_qa.trap: The weak answer is claiming IDoc failures do not impact cash flow because warehouse operations can ship goods without valid schedule lines.

doc_flow.what: A long-term sales agreement established with a customer for a total target value rather than specific physical piece quantities, serving as the master contract for order-related deliveries.
A delivery schedule line generated against the agreement that specifies exact target values and fulfillment dates for the customer.
A logistics execution document that initiates picking, packing, and shipping activities based on the active release schedule lines of the scheduling agreement.
An inventory movement posting that formally reduces stock levels and triggers the cost of goods sold posting in finance.
An order-related billing document created directly from the scheduling agreement that posts revenue to financial accounting.

test_cases.title: Happy Path Value-Based Scheduling Agreement Processing
test_cases.preconditions: Customer master, material master, and condition records for target value exist in sales area 1000/10/00.

steps.step: Create Value-Based Scheduling Agreement
steps.data: Doc Type: MV, Customer: 100000, Sales Org: 1000, Dist Channel: 10, Division: 00, Material: M-VAL01, Target Value: 10000 USD
steps.expected: System generates Scheduling Agreement number and assigns item category WVN.

steps.step: Create Delivery Schedule Release
steps.data: Scheduling Agreement number from previous step, Delivery Schedule tab, target quantity/value for current date
steps.expected: System records release document type LPC and creates schedule lines.

steps.step: Create Outbound Delivery
steps.data: Shipping Point: 1010, Order Number, Delivery Type: LF
steps.expected: System generates Outbound Delivery document and updates delivery status.

steps.step: Post Goods Issue
steps.data: Outbound Delivery number, click Post Goods Issue
steps.expected: Material document is created and inventory is reduced.

steps.step: Create Order-Related Billing Document
steps.data: Billing Type: F2, Sales Document reference
steps.expected: Billing document is created and handed off to FI.

test_cases.expected_result: Value-based scheduling agreement is successfully processed through delivery, goods issue, and order-related billing.
